item.title: France records first human death linked to Shamonda virus
item.description: — Authorities say patient was severely immunocompromised, no public health risk identified France has reported the death of a severely immunocompromised patient infected with Shamonda virus, marking the first recorded human case of the virus. The death was announced on Thursday in a statement by the French ministries responsible for health and agriculture, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP). The ministries described the infection as “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient”. The patient, who died in early October, was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating among animals during the spring and summer. French authorities said clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations were ongoing, adding that no risk to the general public had been identified at the time of the announcement. “Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the statement said. It added that the neurological complications observed in the patient before his death were very likely linked to the infection. About Shamonda virus According to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Shamonda virus is a vector-borne pathogen belonging to the Orthobunyavirus group. It is transmitted to animals by small biting insects. The virus was first isolated from cattle in Nigeria in 1965 and was subsequently identified in other parts of Africa and Asia in the early 2000s. In Europe, clinical signs of the virus in animals were reported from June 2026 and identified in late July, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). The ECDC said the virus had been detected in farm animals in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland, as well as Jersey. The agency said it was working with French authorities and European partners to investigate the potential public health implications of the first reported human infection. Kaseya made the appeal during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, saying the woman had travelled to Uganda, where she spent several days before her husband joined her. Africa CDC warns against blame Kaseya urged African leaders to avoid politicising the outbreak or blaming individual countries, warning that accusations and isolation could undermine efforts to contain the virus. “My plea is clear to all leaders: we cannot play politics with this outbreak; we cannot point fingers; we cannot play isolation; we all need to come together to save our continent,” he said. item.title: Sowore, Basiru clash over 2027 campaign, past activism

The exchange started after the AAC requested the venue for the inauguration of its Presidential Campaign Council on November 11, 2026, alongside food, drinks and logistical support for 5,000 participants, citing equal treatment of political parties. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru questioned Sowore’s political relevance, challenging him to win a seat in a state House of Assembly before expecting to be taken seriously. “Sowore is a skit maker. Let him struggle to even get a seat in the House of Assembly as a politician, and then people will begin to take him seriously,” Basiru said. item.title: Bundibugyo Ebola: Early detection, isolation key to containing Nigeria’s outbreak – Expert
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria must prioritise early detection, immediate isolation, rigorous contact tracing and quality supportive care to contain the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus, a medical scientist has said. Adegboro, who is the incoming Chairman of the Rapid Response Committee of the Academy of Medical Sciences, Nigeria, warned that the absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment does not make the disease uncontrollable, saying Nigeria’s immediate response should be guided by evidence-based public health measures rather than expectations of premature mass vaccination with an experimental vaccine. In an interview, he told Vanguard that Nigeria does not need to embark on experimental vaccination at this stage, given the reported single index case and the ongoing monitoring of identified contacts. Adegboro said the government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), should ensure that suspected cases are identified quickly and tested without delay. item.title: Ebola: Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs
item.description: — State reactivates emergency operations centre, places response teams on standby By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — The Enugu State Government says it has intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following reports of an Ebola case in Nigeria. The state Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, who disclosed this, said no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in Enugu State. “Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said. Ugwu explained that the government had strengthened preparedness measures in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners. He said Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance and preparedness necessary. According to him, the administration of Governor Peter Mbah considers public health security a priority and is taking precautionary measures without creating unnecessary panic. The commissioner said surveillance had been intensified across the 17 local government areas, while coordination with relevant agencies and monitoring around the international airport had also been strengthened. He added that the state’s Public Health Emergency Operations Centre had been reactivated to coordinate preparedness and response, with rapid response teams and technical personnel placed on standby. Ugwu urged public and private health facilities across the state to remain on high alert and maintain a high index of suspicion for suspected cases, particularly among people with relevant travel or exposure histories. He advised healthcare providers to promptly isolate suspected cases and report them immediately to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre. The commissioner also urged health workers to adhere strictly to infection prevention and control protocols, use appropriate personal protective equipment and report suspected infections through established channels. He stressed that early detection and prompt notification were critical to preventing transmission, assuring health workers that the government would continue to provide the support and guidance needed to protect them and ensure an effective response. Ugwu urged residents to remain calm and observe preventive measures, including proper hand hygiene, avoiding contact with the body fluids of sick persons, seeking prompt medical attention when necessary and reporting suspected cases to health authorities. item.title: Customs warns border communities against smuggling
item.description: — Service seizes 1,548 jerrycans of petrol in six weeks By Umar Yusuf, Yola The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has warned border communities across the country against collaborating with smuggling cartels, describing the activity as economic sabotage. The service also pledged to strengthen cooperation with sister security agencies to curb smuggling within and across Nigeria’s borders. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Dr Bashir Adewale, disclosed this in Yola on Wednesday, saying the service would restructure and re-equip Operation Whirlwind, its anti-smuggling unit, and reposition its personnel to tackle emerging challenges. Adewale, who was represented by the National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Deputy Comptroller-General Abubakar Aliyu, spoke during the interception of petroleum products in Yola. He said the service was intensifying its efforts to confront smugglers and prevent the illegal movement of petroleum products out of the country. “The Nigeria Customs has been recording huge successes in its anti-smuggling drive, but the defiant smugglers would not want to give up their nefarious activities. It is on this note that new and harder strategies are to be adopted to face the challenges squarely,” he said. Adewale said border communities played significant roles in identifying and checking smuggling activities, noting that smugglers often operated from communities along the borders. He identified major smuggling flashpoints in Adamawa State as the Malabu–Belel axis, Girei–Wuro Boki road, Fufore–Gurin route, Wuro Alhaji–Maiha corridor and Mubi–Sahuda axis. The comptroller-general disclosed that Operation Whirlwind operatives had seized 1,548 jerrycans, each containing 25 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), in the last six weeks. He said the petrol was allegedly intended for smuggling to neighbouring countries, adding that vehicles used in the operation were also intercepted. item.title: APM denies crisis as South-South chairmen move against Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has denied a split in its ranks after party chairmen and candidates in the South-South reportedly boycotted a presidential town hall meeting in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and passed a vote of no confidence in its presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde. The protest followed allegations that Makinde had sidelined state party structures and failed to consult party leaders, with the aggrieved chairmen yet to decide their position on the presidential election. Reacting to the development, the APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, described the Uyo town hall meeting as a success, attributing the disagreement to misinformation and expressing confidence that it would be resolved. “We are emboldened by the appreciation of the people of the South-South, who welcomed their own with huge support,” he said. The spokesman cited Makinde’s professional and personal ties to the Niger Delta, noting that he had worked in Edo, Delta, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa and Rivers states and married a woman from the region. “There is no problem with the action of the chairmen. We agreed to disagree, even though they have gone too far. It will be resolved,” he said. The Forum of APM State Chairmen in the South-South accused Makinde of running his campaign without recognising established party structures, consulting state leaders or engaging the party hierarchy. Despite the protest, the APM spokesman maintained that Makinde’s campaign remained committed to its Reset Agenda, which he said sought to address poverty, economic hardship and what the party described as maladministration under the current administration. item.description: Foreign nationals seeking to live in the United Kingdom through marriage must meet specific immigration requirements, with some relationships failing to qualify for permission to enter, remain or settle in the country. The UK Home Office assesses applications based on factors including the legal validity of the marriage, the genuineness of the relationship, the couple’s ages and whether previous relationships have ended. According to the UK government’s Immigration Rules, Appendix Relationship with Partner, applicants must satisfy the relevant requirements before they can qualify for permission to live in the UK as a spouse or partner. Although the government does not publish an official list of nine prohibited marriage types, the following nine circumstances may prevent a marriage-based application from qualifying or lead to refusal. 1. Sham marriages Marriages entered into primarily to circumvent UK immigration controls, without a genuine relationship between the parties, can lead to the refusal or cancellation of immigration permission. The Home Office investigates suspected sham marriages and may refuse an application where it considers, on the balance of probabilities, that an applicant has knowingly participated in such an arrangement. Its official guidance on sham marriages explains how immigration applications involving suspected marriages of convenience are assessed. 2. Polygamous or polyandrous marriages that fail immigration conditions Polygamous marriages involve a person having more than one spouse at the same time, while polyandrous marriages involve a person having multiple husbands. The UK does not permit polygamous marriages to be contracted under its domestic marriage laws. However, certain marriages lawfully conducted in countries where polygamy is permitted may be recognised in limited circumstances. Under the Immigration Rules, a person in a polygamous or polyandrous marriage may rely on that relationship for a partner application only if the specified conditions are satisfied. These include restrictions on whether another spouse is seeking or has already received certain forms of UK immigration permission or settlement. Therefore, an additional spouse may be ineligible for permission through the same polygamous relationship even where the marriage was legally conducted abroad. 6. Marriages where a previous relationship has not permanently ended Applicants and their partners must generally demonstrate that any previous marriage, civil partnership or qualifying durable relationship has permanently broken down. Someone who remains legally married to another person, without the previous relationship having ended in a way recognised by law, may encounter difficulties qualifying for a new spouse visa. The Home Office assesses whether the earlier relationship has permanently ended, taking account of the applicable legal requirements and any relevant exception. 7. Marriages where the couple have never met in person Under the relevant partner immigration rules, applicants must have met their partner in person and demonstrate that their relationship is genuine and continuing. A relationship conducted exclusively online, without the partners ever meeting physically, would therefore fail the in-person requirement for this route. Couples who met online but subsequently met in person are not automatically disqualified. They must still satisfy the other applicable requirements. 8. Marriages that are not genuine or continuing A legally registered marriage does not automatically guarantee permission to live in the UK. The Home Office requires applicants to demonstrate that their relationship is genuine and subsisting, meaning it is real and continuing rather than existing solely on paper. Partners will get money from donors. They will implement their activities without disclosing how much they got, without even sending a report to the government,” Kaseya. “And when the outbreak is over, we’ll hear from some capitals that billions of dollars were invested to stop this outbreak.
